question: Something went wrong with this Tamoz runtime in the last few hours. Use the probes to investigate its own record and report the root cause. Set the hypothesis field to exactly one error code identifying the root cause, with no other words or punctuation. Discuss your reasoning and other codes in the findings.

error.message: 402 Payment Required: the account balance is empty

findings.statement: All 6 turns in the 6-hour window completed normally and 30 of 35 effects succeeded; the runtime is not degraded and no turn ended in failure.

The only repeating failure is 4 model.generate.plan attempts, all Tamoz::Agent::ModelCallError with code insufficient_balance, in thread.noise.5 within ~17 ms near the end of the window; each failed on attempt 1 with no retries after.

The only other error code in the window is a single tool.read_file failure with ToolError/not_found in the same thread, occurring after the four model-call failures; it fired once, no diagnose rule matched it, and a single not_found read is a normal miss, not a dependency outage.

The runtime's own rules fired only on insufficient_balance: effect.repeated_failure and model.call_failed, both severity high, category dependency_unavailable, with the rule text noting that an empty account is a provider problem rather than a Tamoz bug.

Earlier threads (e.g. thread.noise.4) show the identical operation mix succeeding in the same window, so failures are confined to the end of the window; the operation-level summary (22 plan attempts, 4 failed; 13 read attempts, 1 failed) matches the per-thread records.

gaps.why: The probes expose only the recorded error code; the inference that the model provider account ran out of funds rests on the code itself, not on a balance reading.

gaps.datum: Per-call request linkage for the failed effects
gaps.why: The failed effects carry request_id null and their created_at values postdate the turn's completed checkpoint in the decision record, so individual failed calls cannot be tied to a specific request from these probes.

proposals.action: Top up the model provider account or install a funded key, then re-run a single model.generate.plan call to confirm the error code clears.
proposals.rationale: Four plan calls failed with ModelCallError/insufficient_balance and the runtime classifies this as dependency_unavailable (provider-side), which only an account-side fix resolves.

proposals.action: Do not re-enqueue or retry the four failed plan effects until the account is funded.
proposals.rationale: The repeated-failure rule advises fixing the one cause instead of retrying; every attempt failed identically on attempt 1, so retries would just reproduce the code.

proposals.action: Take no action on the single tool.read_file not_found beyond normal monitoring.
proposals.rationale: It is a one-off read miss in the same thread, not recurring and not matched by any diagnose rule; only revisit it if it starts recurring.

findings.statement: probe_self_diagnose(360m): in the window there were 6 turns (all completed), 30 effects succeeded and 8 failed; the only failure code recorded anywhere in the window is rate_limited.

All 8 failures are operation model.converse.work_step on thread.noise.5, class Tamoz::Agent::ModelCallError, code rate_limited, each failing on attempt 1 with duration 0-1 ms, between ms 1791141432953 and 1791141432985 (probe_self_timeline(360m)).

The failures are immediate (0-1 ms, so the calls were rejected locally, not after a network round trip) and immediately follow a burst of 5 successful model.generate.plan and 2 tool.read_file effects on the same execution (execution 91914a0d), consistent with a rate limiter (local token bucket or provider 429) being exhausted by the burst.

No other error codes appear in the window: no request failures, no logged worker errors, all 6 write_file approvals were asked and approved (no approval_denied), occurrences 0, journal drops 0, degraded false. Alternative codes (auth_error, quota_exceeded, timeout, context_window_exceeded, approval_denied) have no rows.
Thread.noise.5's turn nonetheless recorded outcome 'completed' despite all 8 of its work_step effects being failed with a single attempt each — the effect failures did not fail the turn.

gaps.datum: Why the scheduler never retried the failed work_step effects
gaps.why: Each failed effect has exactly one attempt; without retry counts or backoff config I cannot say whether the rate_limited failures were transient (would have succeeded on retry) or persistent within the window.

proposals.action: Add retry with exponential backoff and jitter for rate_limited model.converse.work_step effects, and stagger/throttle the burst of model.generate.plan plus work_step calls issued per execution.
proposals.rationale: All 8 failures were single-attempt immediate rejections right after a burst of 7 successful model/tool effects on one execution; backoff and pacing would absorb limiter exhaustion.

proposals.action: Make a turn's outcome reflect failed effects (or at least flag turns that complete with failed effects) in the runtime summary.
proposals.rationale: Thread.noise.5 shows outcome 'completed' with 8 failed effects, so request-level success metrics currently hide this failure mode.

proposals.action: Expose the model-call rate-limit budget (tokens remaining, reset time) in the diagnose summary.
proposals.rationale: The window's only failure signal is the code rate_limited; a budget field would let operators distinguish a misconfigured local limiter from provider-side 429s without reading raw effect rows.

report.summary: Investigated the Tamoz runtime's own record for the last 6 hours via the self-probes. Of 38 effects, 8 failed — all model.converse.work_step calls on thread.noise.5, all with error code rate_limited; the other 30 effects, all 6 turns and all 6 approvals succeeded, and no other error code appears anywhere in the window. The root cause is model-call rate limiting: the work_step calls were rejected immediately (0-1 ms) right after a burst of successful plan/read effects on the same execution, so the limiter was exhausted rather than the provider being unreachable.

Summary: Investigated the Tamoz runtime's own record for the last 6 hours via the self-probes. Of 38 effects, 8 failed — all model.converse.work_step calls on thread.noise.5, all with error code rate_limited; the other 30 effects, all 6 turns and all 6 approvals succeeded, and no other error code appears anywhere in the window. The root cause is model-call rate limiting: the work_step calls were rejected immediately (0-1 ms) right after a burst of successful plan/read effects on the same execution, so the limiter was exhausted rather than the provider being unreachable.
Hypothesis (high confidence): rate_limited
Findings:
1. probe_self_diagnose(360m): in the window there were 6 turns (all completed), 30 effects succeeded and 8 failed; the only failure code recorded anywhere in the window is rate_limited. [from probe_self_diagnose]
2. All 8 failures are operation model.converse.work_step on thread.noise.5, class Tamoz::Agent::ModelCallError, code rate_limited, each failing on attempt 1 with duration 0-1 ms, between ms 1791141432953 and 1791141432985 (probe_self_timeline(360m)). [from probe_self_explain_turn, probe_self_timeline]
3. The failures are immediate (0-1 ms, so the calls were rejected locally, not after a network round trip) and immediately follow a burst of 5 successful model.generate.plan and 2 tool.read_file effects on the same execution (execution 91914a0d), consistent with a rate limiter (local token bucket or provider 429) being exhausted by the burst. [from probe_self_explain_turn]
4. No other error codes appear in the window: no request failures, no logged worker errors, all 6 write_file approvals were asked and approved (no approval_denied), occurrences 0, journal drops 0, degraded false. Alternative codes (auth_error, quota_exceeded, timeout, context_window_exceeded, approval_denied) have no rows. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_timeline]
5. Thread.noise.5's turn nonetheless recorded outcome 'completed' despite all 8 of its work_step effects being failed with a single attempt each — the effect failures did not fail the turn. [from probe_self_explain_turn]
Still unknown:
- The fired-rules and per-operation sections of probe_self_diagnose: The diagnose output is one 14.6 KB line and the display truncates its middle; I could confirm the summary counts and the absence of other codes via recall_output/pattern filters, but could not read which diagnosis rules fired or their evidence rows.
- Why the scheduler never retried the failed work_step effects: Each failed effect has exactly one attempt; without retry counts or backoff config I cannot say whether the rate_limited failures were transient (would have succeeded on retry) or persistent within the window.
Proposed next actions (not executed; ask for one to run it through approval):
1. Add retry with exponential backoff and jitter for rate_limited model.converse.work_step effects, and stagger/throttle the burst of model.generate.plan plus work_step calls issued per execution.: All 8 failures were single-attempt immediate rejections right after a burst of 7 successful model/tool effects on one execution; backoff and pacing would absorb limiter exhaustion. [from probe_self_explain_turn]
2. Make a turn's outcome reflect failed effects (or at least flag turns that complete with failed effects) in the runtime summary.: Thread.noise.5 shows outcome 'completed' with 8 failed effects, so request-level success metrics currently hide this failure mode. [from probe_self_explain_turn, probe_self_diagnose]
3. Expose the model-call rate-limit budget (tokens remaining, reset time) in the diagnose summary.: The window's only failure signal is the code rate_limited; a budget field would let operators distinguish a misconfigured local limiter from provider-side 429s without reading raw effect rows. [from probe_self_timeline]

The ponds.set_aerator effect (effect_key sha256:eb9369d2..., execution 84d5ec04) ended with status unknown and requires reconciliation - the transport died before the runtime could learn whether the external ponds system applied the change. This is the critical rule effect.outcome_unknown.

The failure is isolated to the MCP ponds dependency. In the same window, model.generate.plan (18 attempts) and tool.read_file (12 attempts) had zero failures with sub-millisecond latency, and 30 of 34 effects succeeded overall. Threads noise.0 through noise.4 completed with all effects succeeded (verified thread.noise.4 turn-by-turn).

In thread.noise.5's execution, the healthy effects (3x model.generate.plan, 2x tool.read_file) succeeded first at 1791141432923-1791141432945; the very first MCP call at ...2951 already timed out in 0-1 ms. Instant timeouts on every MCP call, while local tools were fine, points at the ponds MCP transport being down or unreachable rather than a slow server (a real slow server would show elapsed time near a timeout budget).

Diagnose reports degraded=false with no degraded reasons, 6/6 requests completed, and no logged worker errors in the timeline. The runtime itself was not degraded; the recurring-failure rule classified the cause as dependency_unavailable.

Six turn requests all completed, but four tool.websearch.search effect attempts failed, all in one thread, with one identical error code. Every other operation in the window succeeded.
Hypothesis (high confidence): destination_not_allowed
Findings:
1. Every failure in the window is the same: tool.websearch.search raised Tamoz::MCP::WebSearch::EgressRefused with code destination_not_allowed; 4 of 4 attempts failed. [from probe_self_diagnose]
2. Diagnose flags rule effect.repeated_failure, severity high, category dependency_unavailable, count 4, and all four evidence rows are operation tool.websearch.search in thread.noise.5. [from probe_self_diagnose]
3. All four failures are consecutive attempt-1 failures between 1791141921552 and 1791141921564 ms (about a 12 ms burst) in a single thread, thread.noise.5; no other thread had failures. [from probe_self_timeline]
4. Each failed effect has exactly one attempt (no retry loop) and each fails in 0-1 ms, which fits an immediate egress-policy rejection rather than timeouts or an outage with retries. [from probe_self_explain_turn]
5. Everything else is healthy: 6 requests completed, model.generate.plan 18/18 attempts succeeded, tool.read_file 12/12 succeeded, and the thread's approvals show only write_file asks approved (probe_self_timeline shows all 6 write_file decisions approved). [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_explain_turn]
6. The 24-hour view contains the same single burst: no occurrences rows, no degraded flags or degraded_reasons, no journal drops, and zero websearch attempts outside thread.noise.5; the failure is isolated to the websearch egress path. [from probe_self_diagnose]
Still unknown:
- The egress allowlist configuration (which destinations tool.websearch.search was permitted to reach): The probes record effect outcomes and error codes but not the MCP server's egress policy contents, so I cannot tell whether the intended destination was newly added, typoed, or never allowlisted.
- The four distinct websearch destinations/queries attempted in thread.noise.5: Effect keys are hashes; without the arguments I cannot confirm whether all four calls targeted one blocked host or several, though the identical immediate failures point to policy rather than destination-specific reachability.
- Whether thread.noise.0 through thread.noise.4 attempted any websearch call: Their explain records were not pulled; the summary shows zero websearch attempts outside thread.noise.5, so failure exposure appears limited to that thread.
Proposed next actions (not executed; ask for one to run it through approval):
1. Add (or correct) the destination the websearch MCP server needs in the egress allowlist, then re-run a websearch call and confirm probe_self_diagnose no longer reports effect.repeated_failure.: The rule is dependency_unavailable with one recurring code; fixing the allowlist once addresses all four failures. [from probe_self_diagnose]
2. If the destinations in thread.noise.5 were intentional, audit who changed the egress policy shortly before 1791141921552 ms (the first failure).: Failures start abruptly in one thread within a ~12 ms burst, consistent with a recent policy change rather than a gradual network fault. [from probe_self_timeline]
3. No action needed on model.generate.plan, tool.read_file, or the approval path; leave them unchanged.: All attempts on those operations succeeded in the window, so the incident is isolated to websearch egress. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_timeline]

findings.statement: The durable record (runtime.sqlite3) shows no execution failures in the 6h window: 6/6 turns completed, 30/30 effects succeeded on their first attempt (18 model.generate.plan, 12 tool.read_file, p95 <= 1ms), 12/12 checkpoints completed, and all 6 approval decisions were approve.

The runtime flagged itself degraded for exactly one reason: 'the telemetry journal counted 240 dropped signals'. The journal holds 0 documents with 240 drops, so all signals in the window were dropped, none retained.

Every one of the 240 drops carries the same key, tamoz.model.call:queue_full:bulk: the model.call telemetry signal was dropped in bulk because the journal queue was full. No other error class or code appears anywhere in the window - no failed or unknown effect attempts and no logged worker errors in the timeline (truncated:false).

The one probe finding, rule telemetry.loss (severity low, category resource_exhausted), states the durable record is unaffected and that counts derived from the journal are lower bounds - i.e. the visible malfunction is loss of observability, not failed work.

The six threads thread.noise.0-5 are the only traffic; each ran the builder-turn graph v1 normally, and four of them each asked for and received one write_file approval. Nothing in their decision records is abnormal.

gaps.datum: Why the journal queue filled (consumer stall, burst of signals, undersized queue bound, disk pressure)
gaps.why: The probes record the drop class but not the underlying resource condition; the probe's own action note says to check disk space and the journal directory, which are outside this runtime's record.

gaps.datum: Exact timing and spread of the drops
gaps.why: The telemetry.loss finding has first_seen_ms and last_seen_ms both null because the journal retained no documents; the drop can only be bounded to the whole 6h window.

gaps.datum: Whether drops are still occurring now
gaps.why: With an empty journal there is no signal-level record after the fact; a fresh short-window probe would show whether the drop counter grows.

proposals.action: Check disk space, the journal directory, and the journal consumer/worker health on the host running this runtime.
proposals.rationale: 240 bulk queue_full drops with 0 retained documents mean the journal ingest queue saturated and never drained; the probe's action note points at disk space and the journal directory.

proposals.action: Re-derive activity counts from runtime.sqlite3 rather than the journal until telemetry is healthy.
proposals.rationale: The telemetry.loss rule warns that journal-derived counts are lower bounds; the durable database has the complete record (6 requests, 30 effects, 12 checkpoints, 6 decisions).

proposals.action: Raise the journal queue bound or add backpressure/drain alerting on telemetry.loss drops.
proposals.rationale: The drop happened silently as a bulk event and was only visible as a degraded flag; alerting on the drop counter would surface the queue filling before the whole window is lost.
